note: Ps56 'When I am afraid I trust' (corrected; at Gath). Spine = the fear->trust movement: afraid(yare)+trust(batach) paired x3, refrain 'whose word I praise'. Human core: fear overcome by trust, praise of God's word, enemies' trampling/oppressing/attacking + scheming thoughts + lurking/watching/waiting for his life, the tender restless tossings + tears God keeps, confident 'I KNOW God is for me', closing render vows/thank-offerings + walk before God in the light of life. God-qualifiers=5 (gracious, wrath, count+put the tears, delivered). Re-roled tossings/walk/render + oppresses/attack/strife (human) to char; bottle/book/vows/death/falling + enemy-agents to standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: trample / pant after (shaaph - man tramples on me)
paired with the oppression of the attacker

'Be gracious to me, O God, for man TRAMPLES (shaaph) on me' — the relentless hounding that drives the plea; shaaph (to pant after/crush) the enemies' eager pursuit, 'all day long' — the pressure that meets its answer in trust (v3)
oppress / crush (lachats - an attacker oppresses me)
'all day an attacker OPPRESSES (lachats) me' — the crushing pressure of the foe; lachats (to squeeze/oppress) the relentless affliction the psalmist endures at Gath, ground of his cry for grace
the trampling enemies now as warring assailants

'for many ATTACK (lacham) me proudly' — the war waged against the psalmist; lacham (to fight/do battle) the assault of many foes, and their pride ('from on high') — the arrogant hostility that trust answers with 'what can flesh do to me?'
be afraid (yare - when I am afraid)
answered by trust in the same breath

'When I am AFRAID (yare), I put my trust in you' — the psalm's key hinge: fear frankly owned, not denied; yare here the honest fear that does not paralyse but pivots directly into trust — the movement the whole psalm turns on (repeated v4, v11: 'I shall not be afraid')
trust (batach - I put my trust in you)
the trust restated in v4 and v11

'I put my TRUST (batach) in you' — the deliberate act that meets fear; batach here trust chosen in the very grip of dread, resting on the gracious God (v1, the qualifier) — the counter-move to terror, made again and again through the psalm
praise / boast in (halal - whose word I praise)

'In God, whose word I PRAISE (halal)' — trust anchored in the reliability of God's word; halal here glorying in the promise, the refrain (repeated twice in v10) that fear cannot silence — praise as the ground and expression of confidence
the trust of v3 restated, now confident

'in God I TRUST; I shall not be afraid' — trust now settled into fearlessness; batach here the confidence that has passed through fear (v3) to assurance, so that 'what can flesh do to me?' — trust maturing into courage
be afraid (yare - I shall not be afraid)
the fear of v3 now overcome by trust

'I shall not be AFRAID (yare). What can flesh do to me?' — fear conquered by trust; yare here the dread now negated, the fruit of trusting God's word — mortal 'flesh' shrinks to nothing before the God who is trusted
injure / twist (words) (atsab - they injure my cause)
paired with their evil thoughts against him
'All day long they INJURE (atsab) my cause' — the enemies' constant twisting of his words; atsab (to hurt/wrest) the malicious distortion of what he says, the verbal front of their war on him
thoughts / schemes (machashabah - all their thoughts against me)
paired with their injuring and their evil aim

'all their THOUGHTS (machashabah) are against me for evil' — the inner scheming behind the assault; machashabah (plans/devices) the enemies' minds wholly bent on his harm — hostility rooted in the thought-life, aimed at evil
the aim of their thoughts; their crime (v7)

'all their thoughts are against me for EVIL (ra)' — the settled malice directing their schemes; ra the evil purpose of the enemies, the same iniquity named their 'crime' (v7) that God's wrath will answer
stir up strife / band together (gur - they stir up strife)
'They STIR UP STRIFE / band together (gur), they lurk' — the enemies conspiring; gur (to gather/stir) the collusion of the foes, massing and lying in wait — organised malice, not random hostility
watch / keep an eye on (shamar - they watch my steps)
paired with waiting for his life

'they WATCH (shamar) my steps, as they have waited for my life' — the predatory surveillance; shamar here the enemies dogging his every move, lurking to catch him — vigilance turned to a hunt for his soul
wait / lie in wait (qavah - waited for my life)

'as they have WAITED (qavah) for my life' — the patient malice of the ambush; qavah (usually to wait/hope, here twisted to sinister waiting) the enemies' expectant lurking for his nefesh — the same verb that elsewhere names hope in God, here perverted into a hope for his death
life / soul (nefesh - waited for my life)
the same nefesh God delivers from death (v13)
'they have waited for my LIFE (nefesh)' — the psalmist's life, the prize the enemies hunt; nefesh here what they lie in wait for — the same soul God delivers from death (v13), endangered then rescued
the evil of their thoughts (v5), now their guilt
which God's wrath will not let escape (v7)

'For their CRIME (aven) will they escape?' — the guilt that cries for judgment; aven (iniquity) the enemies' wickedness, which the psalmist is confident God's wrath (the qualifier) will not let go unpunished — 'cast down the peoples, O God!'
paired with the tears God keeps

'You have kept count of my TOSSINGS (nod)' — the sleepless, restless wandering of grief; nod (wandering/tossing) the sorrow that turns on its bed at night — and God has numbered every turn, tender attentiveness to unseen anguish
tears (dimah - put my tears in your bottle)
kept by God in his bottle / book
God puts them in his bottle, counts them (v8)

'put my TEARS (dimah) in your bottle. Are they not in your book?' — the weeping God treasures; dimah the psalmist's tears, which God gathers (the qualifier) as precious and records — grief not wasted but kept, the tenderest image of divine care in the psalm
call (qara - in the day when I call)
paired with the knowledge that God is for him

'my enemies will turn back in the day when I CALL (qara)' — the confident recourse to prayer; qara here the calling that puts the enemies to flight — the psalmist's certainty that his cry moves God to act
know (yada - this I know, that God is for me)
the assurance that grounds the calling

'This I KNOW (yada), that God is for me' — the settled assurance at the psalm's centre; yada here not information but confident conviction — 'God is FOR me' — the certainty that turns fear to trust and enemies to flight (contrast the wicked who 'have no knowledge', Ps53)
praise / boast in (halal - in God whose word I praise)
the refrain of v4, now doubled

'In God, whose word I PRAISE (halal)' — the refrain returning, now emphatic; halal the glorying in God's word repeated (v4 -> v10 twice) — praise deepening as the psalm moves toward assured deliverance
praise / boast in (halal - in the LORD whose word I praise)
the LORD, whose word he praises

'in the LORD, whose word I PRAISE (halal)' — the refrain doubled with the covenant name; halal here praising the word of YHWH — the pairing of Elohim and YHWH intensifying the confidence in God's promise
the trust-refrain of v3-4, now closing the assurance

'in God I TRUST; I shall not be afraid' — the trust-refrain restated at the peak; batach here trust confirmed after the assurance 'God is for me' (v9) — 'what can man do to me?', the fear fully answered
be afraid (yare - I shall not be afraid)

'I shall not be AFRAID (yare). What can man do to me?' — fearlessness confirmed; yare negated a second time (cf v4), now measured against 'man' rather than 'flesh' — mortal man reduced to no threat before the trusted God
render / perform / repay (shalam - I will render thank offerings)
vows and thank offerings, to God

'I must perform my vows to you, O God; I will RENDER (shalam) thank offerings' — the vowed gratitude of the delivered; shalam here the paying of what was promised in distress — devotion discharged as a glad debt, not grudging duty
thank offerings / thanksgiving (todah - render thank offerings)
the substance of what he renders

'I will render THANK OFFERINGS (todah) to you' — the thanksgiving that answers deliverance; todah (recurs Ps50:14, 54:6) the grateful offering of the rescued — gratitude become worship, the fruit of trust vindicated
soul / life (nefesh - you have delivered my soul from death)
the nefesh the enemies waited for (v6), now delivered
God has delivered it from death (v13)

'For you have delivered my SOUL (nefesh) from death' — the rescued life, ground of all the thanks; nefesh here the self the enemies hunted (v6), now delivered (the qualifier) from death and steadied from falling — that he may walk before God
walk (halak - that I may walk before God)
before God, in the light of life
the purpose of the soul's deliverance

'that I may WALK (halak) before God in the light of life' — the goal of deliverance: a life lived in God's presence; halak here the daily walk in God's sight, 'in the light of life' — rescue from death issuing in communion, the psalm's radiant close
be gracious (chanan - be gracious to me)
God's grace, the ground of the psalmist's trust (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's grace): 'Be GRACIOUS (chanan) to me, O God' - God's graciousness is not a human IB char; the divine favour the psalmist appeals to and rests his trust upon (280276). Qualifier.
wrath / anger (aph - in wrath cast down the peoples)
God's wrath answering the enemies' crime (v7)

v7 QUALIFIER (God's wrath): 'In WRATH (aph) cast down the peoples, O God!' - God's anger is not a human IB char; the divine judgment the psalmist invokes against the enemies' crime (280307). Qualifier.
count / number (saphar - you have kept count)
God numbers the psalmist's restless tossings (v8)

v8 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'You have kept COUNT (saphar) of my tossings' - God's numbering is not a human IB char; the tender attentiveness that records every restless turn of the psalmist's grief (280316). Qualifier.
put / place (sim - put my tears in your bottle)
God gathers the psalmist's tears into his bottle (v8)
v8 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'PUT (sim) my tears in your bottle' - God's keeping is not a human IB char; the treasuring of the psalmist's tears (280318) as precious. Qualifier.
deliver / rescue (natsal - you have delivered my soul)
God delivers the psalmist's soul from death (v13)

v13 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'you have DELIVERED (natsal) my soul from death' - God's rescue is not a human IB char; the deliverance of the nefesh (280251) that grounds the vows, thanks, and walk before God. Qualifier.
snap at / seize (achaz/shaaph - man pants after me)
v1: the enemy snapping/seizing at the psalmist; a bare hostile act of the foe, the trampling itself carried in the char (280220). Standalone (enemy act).
attacker / fighter (lacham - an attacker oppresses me)
v1: 'an ATTACKER (lacham) oppresses me all day' - the foe as agent; the oppression is the char (280224), here the bare identification of the assailant. Standalone (the attacker).
enemies / watchful foes (shorer - my enemies trample)
v2: 'my ENEMIES (shorer) trample on me all day' - the foes as persons; their trampling and attacking are the chars, here the bare naming of the enemy. Standalone.
trample / pant after (shaaph - my enemies trample)
v2: 'my enemies TRAMPLE (shaaph) on me all day long' - the emphatic repeat of v1's trampling (280220); the same hounding, its 'all day' insistence carried in that char. Standalone (repeat).
proudly / from on high (marom - many attack proudly)
v2: 'for many attack me PROUDLY (marom)' - the haughty manner of the assault; the arrogance carried in the attack char's manner (280271). Standalone (manner).
flesh / mortal man (basar - what can flesh do to me?)

v4: 'What can FLESH (basar) do to me?' - the enemies reduced to mere mortal flesh; the frail-mortality contrast that grounds the fearlessness (280285), not itself a disposition. Standalone (contrast).
v6: 'they LURK (tsaphan)' - the enemies' hiding to ambush; part of the watching/waiting captured in the watch char (280300). Standalone (ambush behaviour).
steps / heels (aqeb - they watch my steps)
v6: 'they watch my STEPS (aqeb)' - the psalmist's movements, the object of the enemies' surveillance (280300); not an inner operation. Standalone (the steps watched).
v7: 'For their crime will they ESCAPE (palat)?' - the enemies' escaping-judgment questioned; the rhetorical doubt that they will evade God's wrath, not an inner operation. Standalone.
v8: 'put my tears in your BOTTLE (nod)' - God's tear-flask, the image of his treasuring the psalmist's weeping (280318); a picture of divine keeping, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
v8: 'Are they not in your BOOK (sepher)?' - God's record of the psalmist's tears; the image of his careful remembrance (280318), not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
turn back / retreat (shub - my enemies will turn back)

v9: 'my enemies will TURN BACK (shub) in the day when I call' - the enemies' rout/retreat; the effect of the psalmist's calling (280329), an outward reversal of the foe, not an inner operation. Standalone (enemies' rout).
vows (neder - I must perform my vows)

v12: 'I must perform my VOWS (neder) to you, O God' - the vows the psalmist owes; the devotion is in the rendering (280246), here the vows themselves as the object performed. Standalone (the vows owed).
death (mavet - delivered my soul from death)
v13: 'you have delivered my soul from DEATH (mavet)' - death as the peril the soul is rescued from; the object of God's deliverance (280251), not an inner operation. Standalone.
falling / stumbling (dechi - my feet from falling)
v13: 'yes, my feet from FALLING (dechi)' - the stumbling/downfall the psalmist is kept from; the deliverance is the qualifier/char, here the falling that is prevented. Standalone (the fall averted).
